pr_body:

#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When comparing EndpointSubsets and Endpoints, we ignore the difference
in ResourceVersion of Pod to avoid unnecessary updates caused by Pod
updates that we don't care, e.g. annotation update.

Otherwise periodic Service resync would intensively update Endpoints or
EndpointSlice whose Pods have irrelevant change between two resyncs,
leading to delay in processing newly created Services. In a scale
cluster with thousands of such Endpoints, we observed 2 minutes of
delay when the resync happens.

@aojea @liggitt @robscott thanks for your comments.
> interesting, this PR was supposed to do that https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/50934

#50934 skipped updating Endpoints by not triggering `syncService` when the received Pod event doesn't contain relevant change. However, `syncService` can also be triggered by periodic service resync and regular service update.

I also agree not setting resourceVersion altogether might make more sense, was just not sure if there was any reason to have it, though its value may have been stale since PR #50934. I could update the PR to remove resourceVersion if @thockin could confirm it's not needed anywhere.

I think that changing the function that compare the subsets is the safest options, it also improves the performance https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/108078#discussion_r805623556 ... and we can always revisit later the resourceVersion field  ... but since we are going to depend on the new function I think we should add unit tests https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/108078#discussion_r805626479

This makes it easier to backport just the "ignore resource version" change if we want to, and also makes sure tests still pass when the controller is encountering objects with resource version set but is ignoring it for "should I update" purposes (which is what the controller will encounter on upgrades of existing clusters)

@thockin Thanks for the review.
> Why does this include Conditions checks?

If it doesn't check Serving/Terminting Conditions, their changes would not trigger EndpointSlice update. It was not an issue previsouly because Pod resourceVersion also changed when any Condition changed, so `EndpointsEqualBeyondHash` would return `false` as long as it checks resourceVersion regardless of the other checks. Since we remove resourceVersion check in this PR, the function should check all fields that matter.

issue_context.title: Long delay in creating Endpoints when periodical Service resync happens
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

We observed a long delay in creating Endpoints for Services when periodical Service resync in EndpointsController happens. For example, one Service was created at “2022-02-07T19:44:59Z” but its Endpoints was created at “2022-02-07T19:47:30Z”, with 2m30s delay. 

We also observed lots of Endpoints were updated intensively around that time even there was no update to their corresponding Services and Pods. The updates started from "2022-02-07T19:44:00Z" and ended at "2022-02-07T19:47:30Z".

It looks like the delay in creating new Endpoints was because EndpointsController was busy updating existing Endpoints. Since there is no update to existing Services and Pods, they should be triggered by periodical Service resync. The interval of resync was the default value: a random value between 12h and 24h.

Normally `syncService` triggerd by periodical Service resync should be no-op because changes that can affect Endpoints should have been processed when the Service or Pod updates were received. There is one exception: if the Pod update doesn't have change that can affect the Endpoints, the update will be ignored and will not trigger `syncService`, for example, when the Pod's annotation changes. However, the Pod's resourseVersion is always updated whatever the change is. Then when periodical Service resync happens, `syncService` will find the existing subsets are not up-to-date and update the Endpoints intensively.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a1ac74224eac04dae21fcee2b32f8e914111ec9f/pkg/controller/endpoint/endpoints_controller.go#L493-L499

The root problem is that some kind of Pod updates (such as annotation update) are ignored by Pod event handler of Endpoints controller while these updates can affect the content (Pod resourceVersion) of Endpoints, so they are accumulated and will be processed together in next periodical Service resync.

### What did you expect to happen?

Periodical Service resync should skip updating Endpoints if there is only Pod resourceVersion update, to be consistent with Pod event handler's behavior, and to prevent normal Services' processing from being affected.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. To trigger periodical Service resync earilier, set `--min-resync-period` of kube-controller-manager to a smaller value like 5 minutes, otherwise the issue will only happen after running kube-controller-manager for 12 hours and before 24 hours, with the default value.
2. Create 1,000 service, exposing same Pod' different ports for simplicity.
```
kubectl create deploy nginx --image=nginx
for i in `seq 1 1000`; do kubectl expose deploy/nginx --port=$i --target-port=$i --name=service$i; done
```
3. Watch the Endpoints object:
```
kubectl get endpoints -w
```
3. Update the Pod's annotation, there will be no Endpoints events.
```
kubectl annotate pod nginx-7cf7d6dbc8-47cgc a=b
```
4. Wait until next periodical Service resync (5min~10min later), all Endpoints will be updated.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_
